clue.text: He advances a chess piece without resources to the right

parts.note: the pawn is the lowliest chess piece
having no money means being broke
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A chess player, short of options, pushes a piece across to the right-hand side of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advances' looks like a chess move, but here it means lending money against goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnshop owner lends cash to customers against pledged goods, so he makes advances.

clue.text: Wrapup forwards

definitions.meaning: to wrap up goods for a journey is to stow them in a case
in rugby the forwards together form the scrum unit

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the forwards, who form the scrum, are known collectively as the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up belongings is to box them; rugby forwards are collectively called the pack.

clue.text: Anything but a rest-home but it did offer some relief

definitions.text: Anything but a rest-home but it did offer some relief

parts.words: Anything but a rest-home but it did offer some relief
parts.note: a Victorian institution where the destitute laboured hard in return for poor relief, the official term for state welfare

explanation.surface: A place that was far from restful nonetheless provided a little comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' is the old word for public assistance to the poor; in Britain the destitute were sent to these institutions and made to work for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorhouse inmates did hard labour, so no place of rest, yet the institution dispensed parish poor relief.

clue.text: Sort of study for a novel school, boy

definitions.meaning: a ... study is a state of deep, absent-minded thought
Tom ... is the schoolboy hero of the Victorian novel Tom ... Schooldays

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what kind of study suits a schoolboy in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown's Schooldays is a classic English novel about life at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown study is a daydreaming reverie; Tom Brown is the fictional pupil at Rugby School.

clue.text: Work on uranium fast to get rich

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Working on uranium quickly to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb meaning quickly, but here it is the season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes wealth and luxurious display, a synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Peer over there just after the start

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman, a peer of the realm
yon is an old word for that place in the distance

explanation.surface: Someone peeks across at something in the distance just as a race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning to look, but here it is a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means at an initial stage, soon after something begins.

clue.text: Tinned meat which upsets the charts

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense, upsetting something turns it over so the letters run backwards

parts.note: charts are maps

explanation.surface: Canned meat that disrupts the pop music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsets' turns MAPS round; 'charts' suggests the hit parade but means maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of canned pork luncheon meat.

clue.text: The bread is mine, thanks

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone claims the bread as theirs and says thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a possessive but is a coal mine; TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow loaf from the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Inclined to tamper with Moslem deed

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up with each other, so the phrase signals they are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone tries to interfere with a religious act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tamper with' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'tamper' and 'with' signals the jumble of MOSLEM DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone meddlesome interferes in other people's affairs.

clue.text: Godly foe disposed to be reactionary

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged differently, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A pious enemy turns out to be politically backward.
explanation.definitionFit: An old fogey is a person with stuffy, conservative views who resists change.

clue.text: It may go by ship and go by car

indicators.note: by here means next to, so one word stands beside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something might travel by sea or by road.
explanation.walkthrough: The last words read literally: GO placed by CAR spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is freight carried in a vessel.

clue.text: Run amok in high spirits, but that is not to the point

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: elated means joyful and excited

explanation.surface: Someone runs wild in high spirits, but it is beside the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amok' scrambles RUN to give UNR, followed by ELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrelated has no connection with the matter in hand, hence irrelevant.

clue.text: Court Lady Luck beside the railway

indicators.note: beside means one part simply sits next to the other in sequence

parts.note: Lady Luck is fortune personified, chance
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone woos Lady Luck next to the train line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a verb meaning to woo, but it is a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Court of Chancery was the Lord Chancellor's court of equity in England.

clue.text: Grow ill after father becomes feeble

indicators.note: after means the first piece follows the second in the answer

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to ail is to be or become unwell

explanation.surface: After Dad falls sick he becomes weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail means physically weak and delicate.

clue.text: Unintentional change of key

definitions.meaning: done by chance, not on purpose
in music a sharp, flat or natural sign altering a note outside the key signature

explanation.surface: An unplanned shift to a different musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by chance is not deliberate; in notation a sign raising or lowering a note is so named.

clue.text: Military take over and permit two lines

parts.note: a coup is a sudden seizure of power, often by the army
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: The army seizes power and allows a pair of lines through.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of successive rhyming lines of verse.

clue.text: Discovering that a listing is about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a list, as of a ship, is a leaning

explanation.surface: Someone finds that an inventory is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listing' looks like an inventory, but it is a tilt, as a ship lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning can mean finding out, as in learning the news.

clue.text: They constantly worry when gangs roaming round return

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters are scattered
return means turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning, and round can mean about

explanation.surface: Fretful people come back when wandering gangs circle round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' can mean about, the Latin RE; 'return' turns that round, and 'roaming' scrambles it with the gangs. 'Worry' looks like fretting, but here means pestering.
explanation.definitionFit: Naggers are people who pester and harass others persistently.

clue.text: A thrifty chap who studies finance

definitions.meaning: a specialist in the science of money and markets

explanation.surface: A careful saver who also researches money matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who spends frugally and an expert in the discipline of economics.

clue.text: Not out to be precise, but not precisely what it should be

definitions.text: not precisely what it should be

parts.note: in cricket a batter who is not out is in
exact means precise

explanation.surface: Someone tries to be accurate but falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter still at the crease is 'in', the opposite of out.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, lacking accuracy.

clue.text: Cultivation of the small shopkeeper era?

parts.note: the till, the cash register, is the small shopkeeper's essential piece of kit
an age is an era

explanation.surface: The days of the corner shop are recalled as a farming time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: the till belongs to the shopkeeper, and 'era' gives AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the preparation of land for growing crops.

clue.text: Shattered door may reveal where students meet in common

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smashed door might expose the common room.
explanation.definitionFit: A day room is a communal lounge in a college or institution.

clue.text: Detective department is in deed determined

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives

explanation.surface: The police detectives are truly resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department; 'in' puts it inside the deed, read here as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Decided means resolute, firmly settled in purpose.

clue.text: Each decimal base has presumably been chewed over

parts.note: the decimal system is built on base ten

explanation.surface: Each base-ten figure has supposedly been mulled over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten has been bitten and swallowed.

clue.text: Search for and find a piece of harness

definitions.meaning: one of the two side straps connecting a horse's collar to a cart

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a strap from a horse's tack.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to locate by searching; traces are the straps by which a horse pulls a vehicle.

clue.text: Place for film making requires skin-protective containing calcium

indicators.note: containing means the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: a lotion is a cream that protects the skin
CA is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: A film shoot needs sunscreen with added calcium.
explanation.definitionFit: Filming on location means shooting at a real site rather than in a studio.

clue.text: I bit the wrong way on a bone

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards

explanation.surface: Someone bit into a bone the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger lower leg bone.

clue.text: One who looks and looks on

definitions.text: One who looks and looks on

parts.words: One who looks and looks on
parts.note: a person who sees, and who looks ahead into the future like a prophet

explanation.surface: Someone watches and keeps watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is literally one who sees, and a prophet who foresees what is to come.

clue.text: A company of old soldiers to teach the regimental brass

parts.note: to train is to instruct
a regiment's brass is its military band

explanation.surface: Veterans instruct the regiment's musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' suggests senior officers, but here it is the brass band.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainbands were citizen militia companies in 16th and 17th century England.

clue.text: She gets the groom to go by horse after a follower

indicators.note: after here sends the riding piece second, behind the follower

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet
to ride is to travel on horseback

explanation.surface: A woman takes the stable lad out riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests stables, but it is the bridegroom; B is what follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride marries the bridegroom at a wedding.

clue.text: Committed perjury for a song

definitions.meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: Someone told falsehoods under oath in exchange for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is telling falsehoods in court; a Lied is a German romantic song.

clue.text: He has to replan terms ahead

indicators.note: replanning means arranging again, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone must rework the timetable for the coming school terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the whole definition: a school's head, who plans terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A head teacher is the man who runs a school.
